quote: Is there a way to email me a quote?
stewart_read: This is a direct match to the script's send_proposal_before_meeting trigger. The rep's reply, "Yeah. Of course. We'll send you an email as well," is a caved_and_promised_to_send response — the schema's own deviation_grades label this a critical_failure, not a soft miss. The rep did not attempt the canonical explanation that proposals require full walkthrough.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read (rep didn't recognize the trigger) is more supported than a strategic one — there is no indication the rep intended to withhold and was managing expectations; he simply agreed to the ask without qualification.
coaching_implication: This is a hard-rule violation, not a style choice. Replay this clip specifically — the manager should treat this as a 'stick to your guns' training moment, since the schema explicitly warns that sending the design beforehand kills the purchase rate.

quote: Yeah. So the way that the program works is it's just a, like, a bill swap. So, like, once the panels are, like, on your roof generating electricity, you'll no longer have that Dominion bill.
stewart_read: This explanation stays at the level of general program mechanics (bill swap concept) without touching prices, specs, or equipment debates — the schema's scope_creep_signals list is specifically pricing, panel/inverter technical detail, or operational debate. This is a borderline case: it's closer-tier content in that it preempts what the specialist call is for, but it does not rise to the severity of the classic scope-creep examples (e.g., SESSION10's inverter debate).
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter reading would call this scope creep outright since it answers a program-mechanism question the closer is meant to own; the more precise read is that it's a mild, low-severity version of it — worth a coaching note but not the same failure class as pricing or spec debates.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the escape hatch here too ("that's exactly what the specialist will map out with your actual numbers") rather than pre-answering, but frame this as a lighter-touch coaching point than the proposal-email cave at 05:00.

quote: And how long does it take to normally pay off a house our size?
stewart_read: Rep's honest admission ("I'm not too sure on, like, the financial side of things. I just work in the scheduling department to get the design started") is transparent rather than fabricated, which is the correct instinct — but the rep stops there instead of using the unanswered question to build anticipation for the closer's call.
alternative_hypothesis: A stricter read would call the honest admission itself a failure, but transparency over fabrication is the correct instinct per knowledge_gap_handling; the actual gap is the missed follow-through into curiosity creation, not the honesty.
coaching_implication: Coach a bridge line here: acknowledge the good question, confirm it's exactly what tomorrow's call will lay out with his real numbers, so the unresolved question becomes a hook rather than a dead end.

quote: I think we we would need you to kinda it'll be about thirty to forty minutes. So I just don't wanna give, like, bad expectations.

coaching_implication: Point out this specific clip as an example of confidence leaking out of a line that should be firm and simple: state the time commitment plainly.

quote: Yeah. I'll be at work with my phone, and I'll be able to pull it up. So Okay.
stewart_read: Customer states he'll take the closer call at work on his phone, not at a computer at home as the button-up script requires. Rep accepts this without re-anchoring the expectation, weakening the setup for the closer's screen-share walkthrough.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep did move the time to accommodate the work schedule (4pm instead of 10am), which is a reasonable strategic trade — but the channel/device mismatch (phone vs. computer) was never resolved, only the time was.
coaching_implication: Flag for the closer: customer plans to take the call on his phone at work, not at a computer. The closer should know to adapt the numbers walkthrough for a phone screen or push again for a computer.
